sections.heading: AUTOMOTIVE & TRANSPORTATION INDUSTRY USES DIGITAL TWIN
FOR PRODUCT DESIGN & DEVELOPMENT
content: The automotive industry is one of the early adopters of digital twin technology. The industry involves
various systems and processes at several stages of the complete life cycle of automobile products and
services. In order to optimize and enhance these systems and processes, the operators in this industry are
adopting digital twins at a significant rate. Automotive product development is complex and time-
consuming. Typically, it takes about 4–6 years for a new car model to be launched right from the design to
the launch phase. Moreover, many new vehicles in the market are equipped with hundreds of sensors for
constant monitoring of critical systems. Effective design is the first and most important phase of the
complete product life cycle, as it can impact the long-term sustainability of an automobile manufacturer.
Even a small oversight in the product design phase can erode the company’s brand value and profitability.
For instance, Mercedes Benz launched its A-Class in early 2000 and incurred a product development cost
of USD 1.5 billion. After its launch, the vehicle failed a Moose test, resulting in the recall of 2,500 new cars.
Subsequently, Mercedes added stability control and redesigned the car's suspension to address the
problem. The cost of implementing the change was about USD 250 million. However, in this scenario, if a
digital twin is built at the earlier stage, i.e., the designing phase, the company can save a lot of time as well

content: A digital twin is capable of analyzing performance data collected over time and under different conditions
during the manufacturing phase of vehicle design. For example, a digital twin enables visualization of a
race car engine to identify the necessity of maintenance of the components that can burn out or get
damaged. Even in the after-sales stage, a digital twin is used for collecting feedback. Digital twins help
ensure the safety of vehicles by monitoring the systems or parts that need replacement and alerting the
relevant teams regarding the necessary change. Also, the manufacturer can analyze the data &
performance through predictive analysis to help make the driving experience smarter and safer. For
instance, Computer Science Corp. (US) partnered with Microsoft Corporation (US) to build machine learning
solutions on an industrial level and used the Microsoft Cortana Intelligence Suite to run the digital twin for
continuously simulating new innovative ideas of creating hybrid cars. Similarly, Cummins (US), a motor

research and development of advanced diesel engines. On the other hand, Faurecia (France), a subsidiary

sections.heading: INITIATION OF SMART CITY PROJECTS TO PROPEL DIGITAL
TWIN MARKET GROWTH
content: The digitalization trends in the infrastructure sector includes edge computing/cloud computing, internet of
things (IoT), and other connected devices such as sensors, detectors, and smart home devices, which have
generated huge opportunities for the future development of cities, buildings, and home infrastructure.
Countries such as India, France, Austria, the Netherlands, Germany, and many more across the world have
undertaken concrete steps for the development of smart cities. Digital twin is highly adopted in smart city
projects as it provides a high-level abstraction on the behavior of the real systems, allowing to know the
real-time status, environmental effects, transfer of information, and, most importantly, the simulation
scenarios. Such inputs and outputs help in analyzing and controlling various parameters. For instance,
Dassault Systems (France) is working on a project in Singapore to create a digital twin called “Virtual
Singapore.” The virtual twin would help urban planners and policymakers visualize the data obtained from
various sensor networks and intelligent systems deployed and to be deployed in the future and use them
to make informed decisions.
Digital twin services are also utilized for digital representation of educational institutes and large university
campuses for energy management, security, digital library management, and other purposes. This unified
image can be used to merge data streams from different building components and create new services.
These can then be used to create new business models and provide real assistance in day-to-day
operations. In addition, the consolidating trend of Construction 4.0, which refers to the fourth industrial
revolution in the construction industry and focuses on digitization, will increase the demand for digital twin
solutions. With the rise in the adoption of Construction 4.0 principles, there will be a massive
transformation in the infrastructure as well as the construction equipment used or controlled

One of the important technologies enabling the creation of digital twins for buildings is building information

of homes such as wireless connectivity, edge computing, analytics, and machine learning are propelling

In the construction sector, a digital twin can be used for capturing the spatial and temporal effects of

economy. The digital twins provide clients with an entirely new perspective on the buildings/infrastructure

new degree of knowledge about a building and how it is operated, resulting in a comprehensive data set
that can be used to carry out maintenance activities based on asset predictive analysis.

sections.heading: GROWING TREND OF DIGITALIZATION IN HEALTHCARE TO BOOST
ADOPTION OF DIGITAL TWIN TECHNOLOGY
content: Digital transformation in the healthcare industry is expected to boost the adoption of digital twins. The
innovations and technological advancements in the healthcare industry have eased the simulation of the
medical devices and monitoring and diagnosis of patients. The use of digital twins in the healthcare
industry will reduce the complexities associated with handling and operating medical devices, such as MRI
and X-rays instruments, and CT scanners. The use of virtual care appointments, wearable wellness apps,
and smartphones as diagnostic tools is likely to increase in the coming years. The IoT-enabled medical
devices approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) are already in use in hospitals to track and
monitor patient status, in homes to manage long-term conditions and medications, and in clinics to
support basic treatment processes. Adopting digital twins of medical systems and processes makes the
approaches to care easy, and these new experiences lead to a rise in patient expectations and enable
doctors to provide continuous medical care to patients.
Healthcare is one of the most promising industries for digital twins. Digital twins are used in
applications/phases such as monitoring, diagnostics, and prognostics. In January 2022, Dassault
Systèmes (France) showcased a digital twin of the human brain at the CES event 2022 in Las Vegas, US.
The company had earlier developed the digital twin of the human heart called the Living Heart, which took
24 months to build. This virtual heart has been generated by combining 208,561 tetrahedrons containing
electrical and muscular properties. Additionally, the doctors at the Bioengineering Institute in Auckland,
New Zealand, have created a virtual lung with 300 million alveoli that function similar to flesh and blood.
Similarly, Q Bio (US), a digital twin startup, offers the innovative Gemini Digital Twin platform for full-body
scan. Q Bio claims that it can capture a full-body scan in 15 minutes without utilizing radiation or breath
holds, and that it can do so using new computational physics models that are more precise than traditional
MRI for many diagnoses. These innovations would help to monitor the organs and provide relevant
treatment in case of any abnormalities.
In addition, the medical device industry has been dynamically adopting digital simulation tools for product
life cycle management across the ideation, realization, and utilization phases of a device life cycle. A digital
twin offers differentiated capabilities at each phase of the life cycle. Digital twins serve as models for
simulation and, thus, enable users to proactively and effectively predict, optimize, and realize the
engineering-based performance and quality of both product manufacturing operations and designs. This
technology efficiently eliminates the errors in medical devices through a data-driven navigational process,
which significantly reduces the issues associated with the quality of medical devices.
A digital twin would help virtualize the hospital system and medical devices to create a safe environment
and test the impact of potential changes on system performance. Apart from operations, digital twins can
also help improve the quality of health services delivered to patients. For instance, Philips (Netherlands)
conducted simulations in the development of a portable oxygen generator for patients with breathing
problems. By using digital prototypes, the company was able to perform tests that would have taken
months and several iterations if it had to build physical prototypes.
A digital twin of a human body could be developed in an organ-by-organ manner, using analytics software
and simulation tools. This will create a highly personalized diagnostics model capable of predicting
upcoming illnesses, recommending lifestyle or dietary changes, and even calculating the age at the death
of a human being. This, in turn, can help find solutions to extend life through healthier living or early
intervention treatments. However, capturing the complex behavior and responses of the highly advanced
organs, such as the brain and neural network, will be complex and critical while creating a perfect human
digital twin. Meanwhile, current advancements are already helping life sciences companies to optimize
their outcomes. Digital human organs are being increasingly prototyped and are likely to become the norm

sections.heading: DIGITAL TWIN HELPS UTILITIES TO IMPROVE PRODUCTIVITY AND
EMERGENCY RESPONSE
content: The demand for energy is increasing and is estimated to grow significantly in the next five years. The
emerging economies such as Africa, the Middle East, and South-East Asia are the major contributors to the
rising demand due to the increasing population, GDP growth, and enhanced access to electricity.
Moreover, there is a shift toward the use of renewable energy sources.
In wind farms, digital twins are being used to display wind patterns, electrical output, and wear and tear on
equipment. They help improve the efficiency of operations. For instance, GE (US) has initiated the Digital
Wind Farm project built on the Predix platform. This software platform creates digital twins of a windmill,
which comprise a digital infrastructure for the wind farm, enabling operators to collect, visualize, and
analyze unit- and site-level data. Through the constant collection of this data, component information,
service reports, and performance data of similar wind turbine models can be obtained from the predictive
model for the digital twin. These predictive models serve as the basis of the new design and simulation
applications, allowing wind farm operators to optimize maintenance strategy, improve reliability and
availability, and increase annual energy production.
Also, the adoption of digital twin technology has created new ways to improve productivity and optimize all
critical parts of production lines in the power industry. For instance, GE (US) developed a software and
hardware system that creates a virtual digital twin of an entire industrial power plant complex. This Digital
Power Plant is powered by GE’s Predix industrial internet operating system, which is a collection of physics-
based methods and digital technologies that are used to model the present state of every asset in a digital
power plant. As the global economy and environment demand real-time control and precision, this
technology enables monitoring and managing every aspect of the power generation ecosystem to generate
electricity efficiently and safely. In addition, GE (US) also built a digital twin that generated 100 million
hours of virtual power plant data and is demonstrated to Aluminium Bahrain B.S.C. (Alba) (Bahrain), which
was planning to build a single-site aluminum smelter that would generate a large amount of ~800
megawatts electricity. The twin of this gas turbine represented how the turbines would react to different

sections.heading: situations in Bahrain.
content: In August 2021, ENGIE (France), one of the world's largest providers of energy efficiency services,
approached ANSYS for simulation technologies to assist ENGIE in making the transition to carbon-free
energy. ENGIE Lab CRIGEN is developing an ultra-fast and high-fidelity platform to deliver the quality of 3D
computational fluid dynamics (CFD) results in real-time, reducing companies' costs, environmental impact
and time to market. Similarly, Doosan (South Korea), a global leader in the energy & utilities industry,
recognized that establishing a digital twin of an existing wind farm would be the most cost-efficient and
effective approach to combine all of the numerous data sources required to understand its wind farm
operations. A wind farm digital twin integrates real-time Internet of Things (IoT) data, as well as other wind
farm and meteorological data, with physics-based and machine learning models to accurately anticipate
output for each turbine in the farm.
Water utility companies employ digital twins to assure a constant supply of water and to be better prepared
for emergencies. They can acquire an accurate assessment of how the current water system functions,
discover issues before they occur, and model what-if situations using digital copies. Water utilities build
virtual models of water systems based on data captured by sensors and actuators in the actual system.
They also leverage data from water industry information systems, including computer maintenance

sections.heading: OIL & GAS INDUSTRY USES DIGITAL TWIN FOR PREDICTIVE
MAINTENANCE
content: In the oil & gas industry, a digital twin is used to predict the behavior of machines, systems, factories, and
processes, which is necessary for future productivity and infrastructure growth. Digital transformation in
the oil & gas industry plays a crucial role in managing, optimizing, and analyzing big data related to plant
operations. IoT analytic platforms are useful in providing real-time analytics that directly drives process
improvements and production optimization. The twin continuously detects and creates new relevant data
to optimize business outcomes. Every smart machine within every system gets connected, after which the
data is sent to communication site links and eventually to the cloud or control centers for consolidation at
the application level. As the digital twin depends on IoT for creating a virtual model, the oil & gas industry
has substantial opportunities to enhance the efficiencies and workflows at a lower cost.
Moreover, these virtual models of processes and assets can be used with knowledge management
systems to train new workers. With the help of smart manufacturing and digital twin, enterprises (Oil & gas
companies) will be able to respond quickly to customer demands, minimize energy consumption, and
improve material usage. Organizations will be able to meet new requirements faster, resulting from
variations in market demand, feedstock, and price. It will also help organizations improve innovation,
productivity, competitiveness, and sustainability.

can cover the data gap in cases when data is unavailable or insufficient, resulting in a predictive digital

sections.heading: FOCUS ON REAL-TIME MONITORING OF CROPS AND AGRICULTURAL
MACHINES TO BOOST DIGITAL TWIN ADOPTION
content: The use of digital twins in the agriculture industry helps in remote monitoring, crop and soil health
monitoring, and livestock and farm management. Digital twin in farm management considerably removes
the constraints regarding place, time, and human observation. The digital twin of a farm or field helps
farmers and other stakeholders to act and take precautions immediately in case of deviations and
emergencies. For example, Dattabot (Indonesia), a big data analytics company, leveraged the Predix
platform offered by GE (US) as its development backbone and developed HARA solutions, which comprise
features such as data acquisition, powerful analytics, and precision agriculture insights. This solution is
designed to transform the agricultural practices in Indonesia in the modern digital industrial age.
Amazon Web Services (AWS) (US) is among the few digital twin providers in the market offering digital twin
solutions for the agriculture industry. The company offers a predictive digital twin solution for the
agriculture industry. The predictions from the digital twin models can be exhibited in context-relevant
visualizations (e.g., 2D dashboard/3D/AR/VR). For instance, in the agriculture industry, AWS offers digital
twin support to Descartes Labs (Mexico), a customer of AWS, that uses satellite imagery to analyze crop
health at a continental size. It also analyzes pricing, supply and demand, and other market data to forecast
commodity markets. End customers utilize these estimates to determine the optimum hedging or trading
strategies, which can result in millions of dollars in savings or trading profits.

sections.heading: 5G COMMERCIALIZATION WOULD FUEL DEMAND FOR DIGITAL TWIN
IN TELECOMMUNICATIONS
content: Product/process/system digital twins can help communication service providers to optimize their network
solutions, processes, and customers services, and how they impact one another. Digital twins can be used
for network design, tower management, and field service management. Once 5G gets commercialized
across the globe, the demand for digital twin solutions is expected to increase at a significant rate.
In the telecommunications industry, a digital twin can monitor and manage complicated telecom networks
while simultaneously gathering data from social media. A digital twin can monitor and augment these
complex systems in real time as operators add layers of technology, such as connected devices and
additional frequency bands. For instance, Nokia (Finland) unveiled the Nokia 5G Digital Design concept,
which aims to emulate 5G use cases. The platform can use digital twin technology to instantly monitor and
assess the impact of 5G deployment while also delivering automated recommendations with the
integration of machine learning algorithms. Nokia also collaborated with digital twin provider Robert Bosch
(Germany) for studying the use of 5G for industrial automation and control systems in manufacturing. As
IoT implementations provide access to large data and broad digital ecosystems, high-fidelity digital twins
are becoming easier to build and maintain. In the future, digital twin technology will be one of the most
important software tools for transforming product development.

sections.heading: DIGITAL TWIN ENABLES TRACKING OF PRODUCT ACROSS SUPPLY
CHAIN FOR INVENTORY MANAGEMENT
content: Digitalization in a retail store does not need personal data and helps optimize the customer experience
and in data-driven marketing that focuses on the individual. In a retail store, operators need to know the
object identity, which enables a marketing function to send marketing and sales messages directly to the
digital twin. For example, a customer with its registered objects in an application will get an alert whenever
a message from a marketing function arrives in one of its digital twins, and the customer or operator can
decide to disable the alert or take access away for the third parties connected to it. At present, object
marketing is one of the powerful new marketing tools for maintaining the balance between vendors and
customers. In addition, object owners can connect with each other to share their product experience by
sending messages among each digital twins created in smartphones. The customers could disable this
community feature as per their needs.
The use of digital twin in consumer goods offers optimized distribution of goods to the customers through
shipment tracking and monitoring, efficient delivery route design, security, and loss prevention.
Additionally, digital twin can facilitate preventive maintenance, a prediction regarding the loss of raw
materials, intelligent consumption of energy, and tracking of assets.
Dassault Systèmes (France), a 3D modelling and digital twin provider, collaborated with Store Electronic
Systems (France), a retail technology business, to create digital twins of retail establishments. A 3D model
of a store's architecture is populated with data from electronic shelf labels to create a detailed virtual
depiction of the store and its contents in the system. The model is updated in real time to reflect the
quantity of items stored on the shelves due to links to the store's inventory and point-of-sale systems.
Dassault Systèmes claims that its approach might be used for a variety of applications, including guiding
shoppers to the products on their shopping list. The approach can also help to optimize merchandise
layouts and prevent stock-outs.

sections.heading: OTHER INDUSTRIES
content: Other industries include the semiconductors, chemicals, paper & pulp, and food & beverages industries.
The semiconductors industry is at the forefront of adopting digital twin technology. The technology is
specifically adopted at the initial stage, i.e., designing and simulation phase, in the semiconductors
industry. In February 2022, ANSYS (US), a provider of digital twins, announced that it will assist LG
Electronics (South Korea) on strengthening its sustainability and digital transformation efforts. To help LG
achieve its goal, ANSYS will offer its CAE and advanced simulation solutions, including artificial
intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML), high-performance computing, and digital twins. Similarly, Siemens
signed a partnership agreement with Bridg (Florida) for creating a digital twin in the semiconductor
manufacturing process. Siemens PLM provided an in-kind software grant valued at more than USD 30
million for the Bridg wafer fab in NeoCity. This digital twin program established the digital duplicates for
model-based systems that lay the foundation for a semiconductor design for manufacturing. The twining
helped Bridg develop its commercialization infrastructure, including capabilities for proof of concept,
custom development, and pilot production.
The chemicals industry has been seeking opportunities to implement digital technologies, which would
help attain operational excellence or offer new products in combination with digital components. The
adoption of digital twins in this industry would help to digitally monitor processing and enable the direct
route for the production of chemicals. However, the timing and scale of impact cannot be predicted, as
these developments in the chemicals industry could fundamentally change the rules of engagement for
chemical production. Siemens AG (Germany) released the STAR-CCM+ software with new features to help
product development organizations to enhance and accelerate software ability. This software is capable of
digitally simulating and predicting product performance in the real world by creating digital twins. STAR-
CCM+ v12.02 is an updated version that includes multi-component gas/liquid species and solid ion
models used to analyze electrochemical reactions occurring in solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs). STAR-CCM+

Food and beverages production consists of complex processes, such as clean-in-place, traceability,
capturing mislabeled products, and sterilization. Along with these, the industry needs to be compliant with
government regulations for food safety, nutrition and health, and sustainability. Smart manufacturing and
digital twin offer food & beverage businesses efficient connectivity, data collection capabilities, and speed.
They can simplify food safety controls by collecting operational data throughout a production environment.
For instance, Bühler (Switzerland), a major developer of equipment (optical sorters and others) for
processing meals and producing materials, is gaining more data and enhancing operations by co-
innovating digital twins to drive digital transformation with Schneider Electric. Buhler has integrated
Schneider Electric's (France) augmented reality application as part of its digital transformation. It used
these augmented reality systems in a test to give customized digital information to machine users based
on their needs. Similarly, Siemens (Germany) demonstrated the utilization of a digital twin in the process
and discrete workflows in the food & beverages industry. The company offers a range of software solutions
that provide digital twin capability across the entire value chain of the dairy industry. Moreover, the dairy
industry is affected not only by factors such as a high cost sensitivity and mass production but also the
growing diversity of available flavors and innovative packaging concepts, which can be overcome using

sections.heading: digital twin technology.
content: Digital twins have become a vital tool for paper manufacturers and machinery businesses that upgrade
their operations in order to meet the rising demand for domestic paper products. The industry faces
various operational challenges such as unscheduled downtime, paper breaks, lack of stability, and a
scarcity of raw materials. In the industry, it is essential for a manufacturer to monitor and manage
workflows and optimize transportation and material storage. This can be achieved through the
implementation of digital twin. Digital twin technology is adopted by other industries for various processes
such as for enhancement of the product development process, optimization of processes, and
improvement of performance of the systems to prevent faults or breakdowns.

sections.heading: INTRODUCTION
content: The digital twin market based on region has been segmented into four regions—North America, Europe,
Asia Pacific, and the Rest of the World (RoW). The RoW segment includes the Middle East, Africa, and
South America. North America has emerged as a prominent region in terms of the development and
adoption of digital twins across various industries such as aerospace, infrastructure, energy & utilities, and
other industries. The region is expected to witness high adoption of digital twin products/solutions in the
next four to five years.
North America dominated the global digital twin market by capturing a share of nearly ~37.5% in 2021,
followed by Europe with a share of 34.0%. The North America market is projected to grow at the highest
CAGR during the forecast period due to the increasing adoption of digital twin in aerospace, energy &
utilities, automotive & transportation, retail, telecommunications, and other industries. The market growth
in the region is also expected to be driven by the growing development in related technologies in the region
such as 5G networking, internet of things (IoT), extended reality, artificial intelligence (AI), and machine
learning (ML). In North America, the US is expected to be the largest and fastest-growing market for digital
twin during the forecast period.

sections.heading: NORTH AMERICA
content: The market in North America has been further segmented into the US, Canada, and Mexico. North America
is the leading region in the digital twin market owing to the increasing adoption of the technology in the
aerospace, automotive & transportation, and energy & utilities industries. In recent years, the development
of various software and deployment of automation solutions in the manufacturing industries have
improved production lines and downstream operations. These developments have positively impacted the
growth of the digital twin market in North America.
Increased R&D in the field of the IoT and IIoT and surging demand for efficient and cost-effective
technologies for product manufacturing are also supporting the regional market growth. Further, the
adoption of automation and enabling technologies in the above-mentioned industries is rising owing to the
need to gain real-time data and visibility into production activities. Key factors driving growth in this region
are rising emphasis on digital twin in manufacturing industries to reduce cost and improve supply chain,
and R&D investments by manufacturers to drive innovation in their manufacturing processes.
North America is a major hub for technological innovations and an early adopter of digital twin and related
technologies. The presence of major digital twin providers in the region such as General Electric (US),
Bentley Systems (US), IBM (US), Emerson (US), Microsoft (US), ANSYS (US), Amazon Web Services (US),
Altair (US), and Oracle (US) also raises the demand and awareness regarding digital twin solutions. These
vendors are investing significantly in the digital twin market. For instance, in August 2021, General Electric
(US) introduced upgrades to its on-premises analytics software, Proficy CSense. The software utilizes AI
and machine learning technologies, along with process digital twins, to identify problems, root causes,
predict future performance, and automate actions.
North America has an established ecosystem for digital twin practices and the presence of large
automotive & transportation, aerospace, chemical, energy & utilities, and food & beverage companies in
the US. These industries are replacing legacy systems with advanced solutions to improve performance
efficiency and reduce overall operational costs, resulting in the growth of the technology market in this
region. Intensifying pressure to reduce costs, growing competition, and the modernization of factories are
the major factors driving the growth of the digital twin market. R&D activities at both academic and
industry levels are broadening the scope of IoT applications in different industries, especially in the US.
This is boosting the market for digital twin in this region. The increased R&D in the field of the IoT and IIoT
and increasing demand for efficient and cost-effective technologies to improve asset performance and
optimize business operation are also supporting the regional market growth. Rapid digitalization across
various verticals, the increasing adoption of smart devices, and technological advancements are fueling
the growth of industrial sensors, digital twins, and artificial intelligence (AI) in manufacturing markets in
North America. The growth of the region is also attributed to the increasing number of SMEs. For SMEs, it is
easier to incorporate new technologies and digitalize themselves. Hence, the increasing number of SMEs
in the region is making it more susceptible to industry automation and digitization.
Furthermore, the electrical transmission and distribution infrastructure in North America is also
unprepared for modern threats and natural hazards. An electrical digital twin enables more flexible and
reliable operations without being affected by these threats and hazards. Moreover, the rising number of
projects related to the integration of renewables, smart cities, smart communities, smart grids, refurbished

In 2021, the US had the largest size of the digital twin market in North America. The market in the US is
further expected to grow at the highest CAGR and dominate the North American region throughout the
forecast period. The US leads the adoption of digital twin in most industries, including aerospace,
automotive & transportation, infrastructure, energy & utilities, telecommunications, retail, and other
industries. The country has been one of the early adopters of digital twin technology. US-based
manufacturers invested in new technologies and disruptive tools and are already seeing the returns on the
investments made. The adoption of digital twin is helping manufacturers in the US to increase productivity,
improve industrial efficiency with better quality control, and mitigate industrial risks.

Increasing demand from automotive and transportation
industries drives digital twin market
The growth of the market in the US is driven by the presence of multiple manufacturers, software
developers, and technology providers, who play a vital role in the development of digital twins. The major
players in the digital twin market in the US include IBM, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services, General Electric,
ANSYS, Oracle, and PTC. These players have started offering products and solutions that help create digital
twins, which form a core part of the digital transformation of various industries. For instance, GE (US) has
built digital twins of critical jet engine components to predict the business outcomes related to the
remaining life of the components. The twins of gas turbines are used to deliver the data regarding the
desired electrical power output at the lowest possible fuel consumption, which, along with the twins of wind
turbines, optimize the process of electricity production from wind farms. These digital twins provide real-
time updated and customized information that enables GE businesses and customers to make timely
decisions and interventions for continued profitability and maximized performance at a low cost.
The manufacturers and organizations in the country are focusing on the digital transformation of their
design operations, especially in terms of 3D designs. Digital twin is one of the digital approaches that
utilizes software simulation tools for creating a 3D model of an asset. For example, the Digital
Manufacturing and Design Innovation Institute (DMDII) has the capabilities, innovative spirit, and
collaborative expertise to transform the American manufacturing sector by offering assistance in the digital
revolution. DMDII has received funds from the US Federal Government for R&D, which aims to
demonstrate tools offered by Siemens that represent the digital twin of interactive kiosks for the processes
ranging from product design to production.
According to the BP Statistical Review of World Energy 2021, the US renewable energy sources, including
biomass, geothermal, hydropower, wind, and solar PV systems, accounted for approximately 17.5% of the
total global electricity generation in 2020 at both utility-scale and distributed systems. The share of
renewables increased by 14.1% in 2020 as compared to 2019, owing to reduced cost and policy support.
The US is the most mature market in terms of smart grid deployment, advanced IT infrastructure, presence
of several enterprises, and availability of technical expertise.
According to the US Department of Energy (DOE), nearly 72% of the power infrastructure in the US is more
than 25 years old, ~60.0% of the distribution poles are 30–50 years old, and ~70.0% of transformers are
25 years old, most of which are approaching the end of their operational life. Aging power generation and
distribution infrastructure, increasing need to deliver clean and reliable energy, and a high focus on
renewable energy generation are among a few major factors leading to increased investments in power
infrastructure. To accommodate this growing share of renewables and distributed energy resources (DERs),
utility operators are planning to invest in the development of digital twin to enhance operational sensing of
their assets and better control power generation and grid components.
The automotive & transportation industry is a major adopter of digital twins in the US. The country is one of
the early adopters of electric vehicles. In addition, in the automotive & transportation industry, Tesla
Motors is using a digital twin solution for every car it manufactures for better performance and business
improvement. Tesla (US), General Motors (US), Rivian, (US), and Lucid Motors (US) are the major
automotive manufacturers driving the EV market not only in North America but also in the global market.
Tesla alone accounted for the highest share in the global plug-in electric vehicle market in 2021. The
overall global plug-in electric vehicle market share enjoyed by Tesla (US) and General Motors in 2021 was
more than 21 %. The introduction of attractive, new options by practically all OEMs, as well as improved
availability of the Tesla Model 3 and Y, boosted sales in North America. Thus, the strong EV market is
further driving the digital market in the country.

Canada is expected to be the second-largest country-level market in North America during the forecast
period. Emerging digital technologies such as mobile apps, digital platforms, and cloud architectures have
increased productivity and innovation in enterprises in the private and public sectors. From the past few
years, the Information and Communications Technology Council (ICTC) has been conducting R&D for
estimating the contributions made by various emerging technologies to the Canadian economy. These
technological innovations are projected to propel the growth of the Canadian digital twin market.
According to Global Affairs Canada (GAC), the country has the lowest cost structures and lowest business
tax burden among advanced economies, with an overall cost advantage of 8.2% over the US and 4.5% over
Japan in the automotive manufacturing sector. This further attracts various companies to Canada, thereby
boosting the digital twin market for the automotive industry in the country. In knowledge-based areas such
as R&D services, which include product testing services, development, and testing, Canadian companies
typically enjoy 27.8% lower costs relative to their US-based counterparts. Such cost advantages are
significant for foreign investors in several industries (e.g., as aerospace, automotive & transportation),
where product development and testing make up for considerable expenses during the development
phase of a product. As a result, Canada offers lucrative opportunities for the adoption of digital twin for
product design & development applications in many industries.
Further, Air Canada and WestJet are two major airlines in Canada in terms of traffic and capacity growth.
These airlines are expected to contribute to the growth of the digital twin market in Canada for
maintenance, repair, and operations (MRO). Additionally, the country is an innovation hub with regard to
breakthrough technologies in the energy industry. According to the Canadian Electricity Association,
increasing investments in the deployment of digital twin would enable utilities to address outage
management, reduce maintenance costs, and improve operations and reliability. Canadian utilities are
expected to benefit from the digitalization strategy as they have a larger network of assets compared to the
number of customers because of lower population density compared to countries such as the US, the UK,
and China. The country is witnessing growth in the adoption of advanced digital technologies such as IIoT,
AI, ML, and digital twins. For instance, the smart meter penetration in this region is about 51%, and the
development in network communication has also ramped up the deployment of digital twin technology in
Canada. Ontario has registered the highest number of smart meter deployments in the country in recent
years and is estimated to witness the highest adoption of smart grid and electrical digital twin
technologies. In addition to electric grid modernization, Canada is emphasizing on increasing its renewable
energy capacity, which would further support the market growth.
Government initiatives for deve loping automotive and energy &
utilities industries to support digital twin market
Mexico is an emerging economy with moderate growth prospects for the digital twin market. It is a rapidly
evolving country in North America. The innovations in and developments of digital platforms are creating
new opportunities for the production, distribution, and manufacturing of assets in the electronics &
electrical and machine manufacturing industries. As a result of these developments, the digital twin market
in Mexico is expected to gain significant traction in the near future.
According to International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), Mexico plans to generate 46.0% of electricity
from renewable sources by 2030. The country is rich in renewable energy sources, including solar,
geothermal, wind, hydropower, and biomass. It is one of the attractive markets for investments owing to its
significant potential for renewable energy sources. With the rising electricity demand, additional
investments in electric power infrastructures, and increasing renewable energy capacity additions, the

sections.heading: EUROPE
content: The digital twin market in Europe comprises Germany, the UK, France, and Rest of Europe. This region
accounted for a share of 34% of the digital twin market in 2021. According to the European Commission,
the European Union (EU) is the largest economy and trading block in the world, and EU members account
for 16% of world imports and exports. Growth in the automotive & transportation, healthcare, energy &
utilities, and infrastructure industries in Europe will lead to the growth of the digital twin market in the

sections.heading: region.
content: Germany, being a global automotive manufacturing hub, is a key market for digital twin in Europe.
According to Organisation Internationale des Constructeurs d'Automobiles (OICA), in 2020, the total
number of all types of vehicles registered in Europe was 16.7 million and was about 9.2 million in the
second half of 2021. The presence of major digital twin providers such as Siemens (Germany), Robert
Bosch (Germany), Dassault Systèmes (France), Schneider (France), DNV (Norway), ANDRITZ (Austria),
Software AG (Germany), and Johnson Controls (Ireland) drives the digital twin market in the region.
The adoption of digital twins in Europe is high at present due to the increasing digitalization of end-user
industries. These next-generation factories in the region have been adopting digital twins in manufacturing
and maintenance activities. Algoryx Simulation AB (Sweden) is working within a European consortium that
addresses the virtual commissioning of smart factories. The consortium is receiving grants from EU for the
past few years to develop standards and tools to enable the implementation of virtual twins of factories.
During the designing phase of the factories, virtual twins are used to design, plan, and optimize the real
factory operations. After the factory is built, the virtual twin is used for virtual commissioning, and
eventually, when the factory is involved in the full production, digital twin is used to monitor, optimize, and

sections.heading: upgrade the factory.
content: In tandem with the European Institute of Innovation & Technology (EIT) Health Germany, European
countries are using digital twins to improve medication prescribing. For instance, ExactCure is a digital
health firm based in France that is tackling the problem of preventing drug side effects. ExactCure
developed a digital twin, a digital clone of the patient based on information such as age, gender, kidney
status, genotype, smoking status, or any other unique aspect that has been shown to have an impact on a
given prescription. This digital twin can then be utilized to simulate drug effects and interactions in
patients' bodies depending on their unique traits. Further, the developments made by European
companies in the area of healthcare digital twin are also supporting the growth of the market in the region.
The European Union makes efforts and promotes R&D programs to aid its manufacturing sector to fully
benefit from emerging digital technologies. Many companies in Europe have implemented digital twin to
improve their industrial functioning, while several companies are making efforts to implement these smart
technology solutions. Hence, smart manufacturing boom in the coming years will create great opportunities
for digital twin providers in Europe.

The digital twin market in Europe for SMEs is expected to grow at a higher CAGR during the forecast period.
The adoption rate of digital twin among SMEs is expected to be higher as compared to large enterprises. A

Companies are attracted to Germany because it is Europe’s largest economy and most populous nation.
According to the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), Germany is the world's fifth-largest economy in terms of

communications equipment, chemicals, medical, and pharmaceutical and healthcare products. With
increasing automation and initiatives for digitization, these sectors act as great enablers for the adoption

of smart factories in Germany are equipped with technologies such as artificial intelligence, blockchain,
industrial robots, and digital twin solutions.
Additionally, the German federal government is promoting and supporting digital transformation and has
undertaken initiatives to incorporate IIoT processes and encourage cloud adoption to increase digitization

simulation of wind turbines operating in a wind farm grid and mandated the use of digital twins in the wind

content: France is focusing on R&D to enhance its technological capabilities and has introduced new solutions to
modernize the industrial sector. Its response toward IoT adoption has been positive. The government has
an ambitious plan to revive the industries based in France with cloud computing and IoT. Technologies
such as IoT and cloud computing play a vital role in the development of digital twins; hence, the rise in the
adoption of these technologies is expected to drive the growth of the digital twin market in France.
Aerospace, automotive, and pharmaceuticals are the most important industries in France. The country is
one of the early adopters of electric or hybrid vehicles. Renault (France) is investing billions in electric
vehicle production facilities to address the increasing demand for such vehicles. The introduction of new
facilities, coupled with government incentives for electric vehicles, is expected to boost the digital twin
market in France. The French automotive industry is continuously making efforts to increase
competitiveness by reducing costs and increasing productivity through automation. The French
government planning to have one million electric and hybrid vehicles on the road by 2022; subsequent
investments in vehicle manufacturing are expected to boost the market for digital twin for designing &
development of auto parts, predictive maintenance, and other applications.
The country has set ambitious green energy targets for renewable energy adoption and development of EV
charging infrastructures to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050. According to International Renewable
Energy Agency (IRENA) 2021, France installed a solar energy capacity of 929 MW and wind capacity
additions of 955 MW in 2020. The share of renewable energy in the country’s energy mix is growing,
representing 25.3% of France’s gross final energy consumption for 2022. With the increasing adoption of
renewable energy sources, there has been a significant strain on the country’s grid operators to provide
reliable power and accommodate fluctuations in power supply and bi-directional flow of power.
Steady development of renewable energy infrastructure and
adoption of 5G and IoT to drive market growth
According to the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), the UK is the third-largest economy in Europe, with its
manufacturing industry accounting for ~10% of its economic output. The UK government, in its budget for
2020, announced that the corporation tax main rate (for all profits except ring fence profits) would be 19%
for the fiscal years beginning April 1, 2020, and 2021, thus making the environment for industries more

sections.heading: favorable.
content: The UK has played an integral role in the evolution of industrial operations. The IoT is considered as the
prime driver for the next industrial revolution. The UK government has appointed the Ordnance Survey
(UK), the national mapping agency for the UK, to generate a smart map comprising a digital twin that would
determine the best locations for the radio antennae needed to establish a 5G network. Thus, the growing
adoption of new technologies with digitization is expected to boost the economic growth of the UK, and
consequently drive the growth of the digital twin market in the near future.
In June 2021, Samsung (South Korea) announced its entry in Europe with a Vodafone (UK) 5G network
deal. Vodafone, a British telecommunication company, chose Samsung Electronics to supply its 5G
network equipment in the UK under a new agreement. With the advent of 5G connectivity, the market for
digital twins is expected to not only flourish in the UK but also across the entire European region. AI is
required for a fully operational and efficient 5G network. The use of 5G networks allows for the integration

of machine learning and AI at the network edge. 5G allows multiple IoT devices to connect at the same
time, generating a massive amount of data that must be processed using machine learning and AI.
The phasing out of coal and increasing investments in wind and solar power generation are expected to
increase direct investments in the upgrade of transmission and distribution networks in the UK. According
to the UK Department for Business, Energy, and Industrial Strategy, the UK government plans on
implementing digital energy strategies to reduce capital expenditure and operational cost of power
projects, optimize power sector operations, and asset performance management. Power utilities in the UK
apply advanced digital technologies, such as IoT, AI, blockchain, and digital twin, to enable high
interoperability of data, flexible processes, and asset performance management.

sections.heading: REST OF EUROPE
content: Rest of Europe includes the Netherlands, Norway, Spain, Italy, Sweden, Belgium, and Scandinavian
countries. The region accounts for a significant share of the European digital twin market and is expected
to grow at a significant CAGR during the forecast period.
Spain is one of the developed countries in Europe, and the automotive industry is one of the key
contributors to the overall economy of Spain. Most of the country’s automotive products are exported (to
~130 countries). Many major automobile manufacturing companies are based in Spain. All these
manufacturers focus on leveraging industrial automation and communication technologies/products to
ensure greater production efficiency. Among all the European countries, the industrial 3D printing market
in Spain is expected to grow at the fastest rate during the forecast period. Government support and

sections.heading: growth in China
content: China is a key country-level market in the Asia Pacific region. According to the International Trade Centre,
China is the world’s largest exporter and importer of manufactured goods. The growing population has
resulted in the growth of several industries, such as electronics, automotive & transportation,
telecommunications, energy & utilities, and other industries. Thus, China is the largest market for digital
twins that are mainly utilized in the electronics, automotive, and telecommunications end-user industries.
The country is one of the major manufacturing hubs in the world. The Chinese government is actively
adopting new and improved manufacturing strategies to develop its manufacturing sector, and reform and
strengthen various industries. IIoT is increasingly being adopted in China owing to the heavy financial and
strategic involvement of the government in R&D of IoT-based solutions. The Government of China is
committed to developing the nation’s IIoT capabilities. As China is a major hub for semiconductor
fabrication and manufacturing industries, its involvement in the implementation and development of IIoT is
crucial for the growth of these industries. The government is actively adopting new and improved strategies
to develop its manufacturing sector and reform and strengthen other industries. Growing adoption of
automation technologies and government support to spur industrialization are expected to drive the growth
of the digital twin market.
The government is working toward implementing the Made in China 2025 program, a 10-year government-
sponsored program aimed at putting China on equal footing with Western industrial countries. The plan is
focused on automation and the development of cyber-physical systems that will boost lean production and
cut dependency on an outdated cheap-labor model. The continuously increasing labor costs in the country
is prompting companies, such as Foxconn Technology Company Limited (Taiwan), to work on developing
industrial robots, targeting about ~50% automation in Chinese factories by 2022. Government support
encourages end users to adopt digital twin solutions to enhance operational efficiency.

manufacturing to fuel market growth
Being the first country to be industrialized in Asia Pacific, Japan has a competitive advantage over other
countries in the region. Japan’s major exports include automobiles, consumer electronics, semiconductors,
and iron and steel, among others. Lean manufacturing or just-in-time manufacturing is a manufacturing
trend that emerged in Japan and is popular with major manufacturing companies in the country as well as
globally. As quality has always been the priority for Japan-based manufacturers, their products have a high
value in the global market. The country has now launched the Industrial Value Chain Initiative to explore
Industry 4.0 options across the manufacturing sector. Members of this initiative include major businesses
in the electric, IT, machinery, and automobile sectors, including Mitsubishi Electric, Fujitsu, Nissan Motor,

sections.heading: and Panasonic.

Toshiba Corporation (Japan) released SPINEX, a new IoT architecture that combines the latest technologies
of the Toshiba Group with the experience and expertise of a wide range of industries and worksites,
including the energy, social infrastructure, and manufacturing fields. SPINEX is a collection of industrial IoT

According to the Japanese government’s panel on future investment, post the outbreak of COVID-19, there
is a need for the shift of the manufacturing base of high value-added products to the country and other
goods across Southeast Asia. This shift will lead to an upsurge in the demand for digital twins in new
facilities during the forecast period.
Further, the government has made several policy reforms to accelerate the decarbonization of the energy
sector and reduce dependency on fossil fuel-fired power generation. In July 2021, the government
released a draft of the revised Strategic Energy Plan, which proposed a target of a 36–38% share of
renewables and a 20–22% share of nuclear power in the country’s energy mix by 2030. Such large-scale
investments in renewable energy and strengthening policy support in the coming years are likely to boost
the adoption of digital technologies such as digital twins to improve operational flexibility.
Rising government initiatives for smart manufacturing to boost
digital twin market in India
The Government of India is encouraging foreign players to establish their manufacturing plants in India to
encourage the development of the Indian manufacturing industry with the help of state-of-the-art
manufacturing technologies offered by the players operating globally. Thus, this initiative by the
government is encouraging foreign players to invest in the manufacturing industry in India, which would
increase the adoption of digital twin technology in new plants, leading to the growth of the digital twin
market in this region.
The National Manufacturing Policy, an initiative by the Indian government, aims to increase the share of
manufacturing in GDP to 20% by 2025, which will lead to an increase in manufacturing activities in the
automation sector and fuel the requirement for power. Such initiatives and developments in India are
expected to increase the implementation of digital twins for power supplies in the near future.
In the recent past, the government has come up with various initiatives supporting the growth of the
manufacturing industry. The government intends to increase this contribution further by adopting
advanced industrial automation technologies and developing related infrastructure. The “Make in India”
initiative is designed to help manufacturing industries grow and compete globally. The “Digital India”
initiative is expected to increase internet penetration in the country, with companies such as Google (US)
and Facebook (US) lending their technical expertise toward the expansion of internet connectivity. Another
initiative spearheaded by the Ministry of Heavy Industries is “Samarth Udyog Bharat 4.0,” with the aim of
accelerating the adoption of smart manufacturing solutions through knowledge sharing, increasing
awareness, and contextual solution creation in India. The role of the government to promote the adoption
of advanced technologies in the country is increasing industrial automation in India, which is consequently
projected to boost the growth of the smart manufacturing market. This, in turn, is expected to drive the
market for digital twin in India.
India’s power system is undergoing a transformation towards cleaner electricity. The country has set an
ambitious national-level renewables target of 175 GW by 2022 and a national renewables ambition of
increasing its capacity to 450 GW by 2030. However, according to the International Energy Agency, as of
2020, conventional generation still dominated India’s capacity mix, with coal and lignite accounting for
205 GW (55%) and gas representing 25 GW (7%) of the total capacity. To support the integration, the
country plans to develop Green Energy Corridors that support the massive renewable energy capacity
addition targets. The rising penetration of renewable energy, both at utility scale and in decentralized
mode, would necessitate the implementation of digital technologies such as digital twins for better
forecasting and asset management in India. Also, digital twin technologies can help overcome the poor grid
connectivity and transmission losses in the country by improving the quality and supply of power. For

content: According to the Ministry of Mines and Energy of Brazil, the country’s installed power generation capacity is
projected to reach 212.5 GW by 2024. The ministry also stated that an investment of USD 531.0 billion is
required by 2024 to modernize the power infrastructure in the country and is expected to add 15 GW of
centralized power generation capacity by 2025. The government plans to invest USD 62 billion in utilized-
scale power generation and USD 10 billion in distributed generation by 2029. Furthermore, total
investments in the power transmission sector are projected to reach USD 22 billion by 2029, with USD 15
billion allocated to the expansion and upgrade of transmission lines and USD 7 billion in substations. In
addition, according to the Brazilian Energy Planning Agency´s (EPE) Energy Expansion Plan (PDE) for
2019–2029, the country plans on increasing the renewables capacity and is targeting a share of 48% in
the power generation mix by 2029. The integration of renewables and management of distributed energy
resources are expected to provide ample opportunity to technology vendors providing IoT, AI, AR, and
digital twin solutions. The government is investing in biomass power generation, solar power generation,
thermal power generation, and offshore wind power generation to mitigate the risk of power shortages
during periods of severe drought. It has set a target to deploy 3.5 GW and 7 GW of solar PV power plants by
2023 and 2024, respectively. Thus, increased government investments to upgrade the power
infrastructure of Brazil is expected to fuel the growth of the digital twin market in the country.
In addition, the increase in aircraft deliveries and the high demand for MRO services in this region are
expected to be the key factors driving the growth of the digital MRO market in Africa. Leading airlines in
this region are adopting MRO for fleet maintenance, which, in turn, is projected to drive the growth of the
digital twin market in Africa.

sections.heading: PRODUCT/SOLUTION PORTFOLIO
content: The top companies offer digital twin product/solution for both large enterprises and small & medium
enterprises. These companies have invested in R&D to offer high-quality digital twin platforms, software
solutions, and excellent services across the world. With the advent of 5G technology, growing deployment
of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) algorithms, and increasing focus on digital twins for
predictive maintenance, digital twin providers are now focusing on providing specialized digital twin for the
healthcare industry. Digital twin in healthcare enables to better understand disease development in
patients over time and understand the response to new medications, therapies, or surgical interventions.
For instance, Siemens Healthineers is developing a digital twin of the heart to help with pharmacological
therapy and cardiac catheterization simulations. Similarly, Dassault Systèmes’ Living Brain project is
guiding epilepsy therapy and tracking the evolution of neurodegenerative illnesses. Similar projects have
been conducted for the lungs, knees, eyes, and other human organs by the company.

thereby providing excellent reach to their clients. General Electric (US), Microsoft (US), Amazon Web
Services (US), and Dassault Systèmes (France) have major presence in North America and significant
presence in Asia Pacific, Europe, and the Rest of the World. Siemens (Germany) has major presence in
Europe, and strong presence in North America, Asia Pacific, and the Rest of the World.

sections.heading: MARKET SHARE ANALYSIS, 2021
content: The digital twin market witnessed exponential growth in 2021 as compared to 2020. Since 2021, the
market for digital twin has seen significant growth, which continued throughout 2021. The increasing
automation and Industry 4.0 developments escalated the demand for digital twin solutions in the
healthcare, automotive & transportation, infrastructure, telecommunications, and other industries. The
demand from the healthcare industry is driven by growing use cases of digital twins. Through the digital
twin solutions, the efficacy and interactions of medications in the body of a patient based on their personal
characteristics such as age, gender, kidney status, and others are monitored. With the rapid spread of the
coronavirus, healthcare and pharmaceuticals industries are at the forefront of combating COVID-19 with
digital twin applications. Further, the technology is used widely for predictive maintenance across various
industries. Digital twin-based predictive maintenance uses real-time sensor records about the health and
working conditions of a product, process, or system/unit and analyzes it against historical data about its
failure modes and their criticality. This section provides a market share analysis of the top companies
offering digital twin products/solutions.

content: Microsoft focuses on bringing these digital twins to life with a live execution environment that tracks twin
evolution. In addition, powerful query APIs also provide meaningful insights into the behavior of simulated
settings, and it connects with Azure data analytics that helps in creation of a powerful digital twin to
optimize the businesses of the clients. Microsoft is developing new digital tools, which will enable its cloud-
connected machines to predict the exact point at which an equipment needs maintenance, averting
possible breakdowns. Many industrial manufacturers are leveraging the capability of HoloLens to develop a
virtual service business, which allows senior technicians to guide other technicians remotely across the
globe. This gives the company a competitive advantage in the digital twin market. The company also spent
about 12% to 13% of its revenue every year in the last three years for the development of innovative

sections.heading: SIEMENS
content: Siemens is a global technology provider that specializes in manufacturing, infrastructure, transportation,
and healthcare. Siemens operates through the following reportable business segments: Digital Industries,
Smart Infrastructure, Siemens Healthineers, Mobility, Portfolio Companies, Siemens Financial Services,
and Reconciliation to Consolidated Financial Statements.
Siemens works on making digital twins more accessible to consumers and reducing the time it takes to
develop and adapt them. To this end, the company devised the Digital Twin Operations (DT Ops) strategy.
With DT Ops, the digital twin is approached in a modular manner. It contains best practices and tools for
managing the lifecycles of digital twins by combining modelling and simulation of digital twins (DT) with IT
operations (Ops). The company continues to invest in R&D for Product Digital Twins (using digital twins for
efficient design of new products), Production Digital Twins (using digital twins in manufacturing &
production planning), and Performance Digital Twins (using digital twins capture, analyze, and act on
operational data). Siemens has extensive experience in development of key components of digital twin
such as IoT, artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), as well as other high-end digital software and
related technologies that work in tandem with digital twins. Siemens has also invested in the creation of
digital twin for additive manufacturing factories.

sections.heading: Business overview
content: General Electric (GE) is a technology and financial services company involved in the development and
manufacturing of products that are used in the generation, transmission, distribution, control, and
utilization of electricity. The company operates through the Aviation, Healthcare, Power, Renewable Energy,
and Corporate segments. GE conducts its business in the areas of additive manufacturing, aviation,
capital, digital, healthcare, power, renewable energy and research, and licensing.
The Corporate segment comprises the earnings of the Global Research Center and GE Digital business, as
well as the remaining GE Capital operations, including the run-off Insurance business. The company offers
its Digital Twin Creation service via the GE Research division located in Niskayuna, New York, US. GE
Research is the research and development division of General Electric. Through its Digital Twin Creation,
GE builds complex physical assets that are crucial to critical infrastructure, such as energy generation and
distribution, air and train transportation, and healthcare. The company builds digital twins for applications
in several industries, including aerospace, power & utilities, and automotive & transportation.
The business model of GE focuses on the development of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) ecosystem.
The company has started developing industrial software solutions based on big data under its Intelligent
Platforms division. The company is one of the founding members of the Industrial Internet Consortium,
which is a non-profit organization. In 2016, GE Digital, a US-based subsidiary of General Electrics, made its
Predix platform operational for the first time. The Predix platform is a digital software solution for various
industries such as telecommunications, power, manufacturing, oil & gas, and mining. GE’s digital twin
software uses machine learning and advanced analytics to monitor vast amounts of industrial data in real
time, including HMI/SCADA systems, time series, alarms, events, and weather and ambient temperature
readings. GE Digital, the US-based subsidiary of General Electric, provides digital twin platforms and digital
twin software for analytics orchestration and execution of digital twin technologies. GE provides more
dimensionality to increase the performance of the asset or system modeled using GE’s digital twin. The GE
digital twin incorporates the fundamental physics of GE systems, including steady-state and dynamic
behavior, as well as how to effectively provide the desired outcome. The GE Digital Twin footprint extends
into the embedded control layer. As of December 2021, the company claimed the completion of 50,000
units of single Predix Edge customer deployment across the globe, with almost 400 billion data points

content: K e y  s t r e n g t h s / r i g h t  t o  w i n
General Electric's strength is its global business network, which enables it to offer high-quality digital twin
platforms, software solutions, and excellent services in locations all over the world. By leveraging its
network, General Electric can anticipate and elicit a wide range of customers' needs. GE offers the Digital
Twin Framework (GENIX) platform that helps to build digital twins for client’s specific business needs.
GENIX makes it possible to create digital twins that represent a single asset, an integrated system of
assets, or a fleet of assets. Cloud-based digital twins become a single source of truth for all information
about an asset, including data about its history and present state, condition, and performance.
General Electric has continuously made innovations in its products and solutions. For instance, the
company expanded its digital twin portfolio with the launch of the latest version of its Proficy Historian
2022 offering with updates such as tag mapping and advanced trend analysis. Similarly, GE also updated
its SmartSignal software solution with the release of its new version in April 2021. The new version of
SmartSignal digital twin solution enables industrial end users to predict, diagnose, forecast, and prevent
downtime of critical equipment.
GE offers solutions for the overall digital twin ecosystem that work in tandem and are well interlinked with
each other. For instance, GE offers Digital Ghost, which is a real-time, active cyber defense for securing
industrial assets and critical infrastructure from both malicious cyber-attacks and naturally occurring faults.
Critical assets in today's power plants, such as gas turbines, are all governed by physics, which GE fully
comprehends and uses to develop digital twins of these equipment. Digital Ghost, on the other
hand, continuously monitors the asset's activity using these digital twins, knowledge of the underlying
control systems, and very advanced artificial intelligence algorithms. Even though the operator's user
interface suggests everything is fine, the Digital Ghost can recognize if the machine is behaving abnormally
due to a cyber-attack.
S t r a t e g i c  c h o i c e s  m a d e
GE has strengthened its position in the market by investing in technology, globalization, partnerships,
acquisitions, and agreements. The company has been investing in disruptive innovation, which is likely to
improve its industrial productivity in the future. For instance, in January 2022, GE Digital, a subsidiary of
General Electric, launched the GE Proficy Historian 2022, a historian software solution that collects
industrial time-series and alarms & events (A&E) data to analyze asset and process performance to drive
business value. Predix MDC will allow manufacturers with operational analysis to reduce the size of on-

premises systems and make them run more efficiently. Proficy Historian 2022 features a flexible and
scalable design—from sensor to enterprise—that makes it ideal for industrial internet deployments. For
instance, GE's Proficy Historian can help to create a single industrial data repository across the client’s
entire plant for improved visibility and insights, resulting in increased plant capacity. A global chemical
company used GE's Proficy Historian solution to increase its capacity by 20%. Similarly, GE's Proficy
Historian can help large power monitoring and diagnostics centers to save tens of millions of dollars with a
reduction in unplanned downtime and IT infrastructure costs.
With the expansion of several new developments in several software suits and Predix platform in the last
three years, General Electric aims to capitalize on its strengths in the digital twin business to maintain its
position as one of the global leaders in the digital twin market. GE is also focusing on inorganic growth
strategies to enhance its digital twin market position. For instance, in December 2021, GE Digital acquired
Opus One Solutions Energy (US) to accelerate the adoption of renewables and distributed energy resources
(DERs) at all points on the grid. The acquisition will bring together a skilled team of Opus One engineers
and management dedicated to grid innovation, as well as a century of continuous GE innovation. This
combined effort will create an interoperable portfolio that will assist utilities in forecasting, managing,
optimizing, and trading renewable energy. Moreover, General Electric is making investments in Egypt to
launch new renewable projects. The company should focus on expanding its presence in the Middle East &
Africa, as the logistics and mining industries are witnessing healthy growth in these regions. Digital twins
are used in these industries to reduce design iterations, optimize storage locations, compress schedules,
and reduce production costs.
W e a k n e s s e s  a n d  c o m p e t i t i v e  t h r e a t s
The company experienced a decline of 2.2% in revenue in FY 2021 over FY 2020, owing to the impact of
rising inflationary costs of transportation and commodities on various industries. GE has operations in
nearly every country, serves clients in over 175 countries, and the company generated ~56% of its revenue
outside the US in 2021. As a result of dense global network, GE’s sales are affected by local and regional
economic environments and policies in the US and other markets that the company serves, including
interest rates, interest rates, monetary policy, inflation, economic growth, recession, commodity prices,
currency volatility, currency controls or other limitations on the ability to expatriate cash, sovereign debt
levels and actual or anticipated defaults on sovereign debt in the Middle East & Africa. The company can
focus on pursuing strategic alliances to expand its partner network in the region. Short-term demand
fluctuations amid an uncertain market outlook may hamper the revenue generation of the company. In
addition, the effect of above-mentioned risks continues to be heightened by the impact of the COVID-19
pandemic in 2021. As a result, the growth of the digital twin market also stagnated to some extent in 2020
and continued to remain impacted in 2021–22 with a slower growth rate as compared to predicted growth
rate by GE in the absence of COVID-19. GE faces fierce competition to retain existing clients, as new
emerging players are performing well with innovative product launches in the field of digital solutions. A
few of the major competitors of GE are IBM (US), Microsoft (US), and Robert Bosch (Germany).

environments such as factories, farms, energy networks, buildings, stadiums, railways, and cities. It uses
models that employ the Digital Twins Definition Language (DTDL) to describe twins in terms of their
components, state attributes, instructions, telemetry events, and relationships. With an open modeling
language, users can easily model and construct digital representations of networked settings. Model cities,
factories, farms, energy networks, railways, stadiums, and even entire cities can be created with the help
of digital twin, modeling language, and simulation. Microsoft focuses on bringing these digital twins to life
with a live execution environment that tracks twin evolution. In addition, powerful query APIs also provide
meaningful insights into the behavior of simulated settings, and it connects with Azure data analytics that
helps in creation of a powerful digital twin to optimize the businesses of the clients.
Microsoft is developing new digital tools, which will enable its cloud-connected machines to predict the
exact point at which an equipment needs maintenance, averting possible breakdowns. Many industrial
manufacturers are leveraging the capability of HoloLens to develop a virtual service business, which allows
senior technicians to guide other technicians remotely across the globe. This gives the company a
competitive advantage in the digital twin market. The company also spent about 12% to 13% of its revenue
every year in the last three years on the development of innovative solutions. It has more than 10,000
patents in its digital solution for Azure portfolio.
