sections.heading: Business overview
content: Siemens is a global technology provider that specializes in manufacturing, infrastructure, transportation,
and healthcare. Siemens operates through the following reportable business segments: Digital Industries,
Smart Infrastructure, Siemens Healthineers, Mobility, Portfolio Companies, Siemens Financial Services,
and Reconciliation to Consolidated Financial Statements. The company focuses on areas such as
electrification, automation, and digitalization. Siemens allows its customers to improve their businesses by
connecting the physical and digital worlds, enabling them to create actual value for clients.
The company offers cloud-based engineering solutions that connect users with a private cloud. Users can
access the plant controller with the help of the totally Integrated Automation (TIA) Portal Cloud Connector,
or via MindSphere (cloud solution by Siemens) for additional digital services offered by Siemens.
Additionally, PLCSim Advanced with interfaces is used as simulation software such as Plant Simulation and
Process Simulation. A Simatic S7-1500 controller can be simulated as a digital twin with PLCSim Advanced
to achieve efficient virtual commissioning. The digital twin offerings by Siemens are not confined to one
particular business segment of the company. The Smart Infrastructure segment of Siemens continues to
promote the digitalization of its switching and control products with built-in intelligence, cloud connectivity,
and more remote diagnostics and edge computing capacity. Siemens digital twins of products, building
systems, and grids provide customer values from online configuration and parametrization to operation
and maintenance planning. Similarly, the Siemens Mobility segment develops efficient vehicle platforms
with low lifetime costs and maximum customization options with continuous R&D investments in
connectivity, simulation, digital twin, data analytics and AI, additive manufacturing, and software systems

sections.heading: and processes.
content: Siemens works on making digital twins more accessible to consumers and reducing the time it takes to
develop and adapt them. To this end, the company devised the Digital Twin Operations (DT Ops) strategy.
With DT Ops, the digital twin is approached in a modular manner. It contains best practices and tools for
managing the lifecycles of digital twins by combining modeling and simulation of digital twins (DT) with IT
operations (Ops). Individual components are scalable and reusable, allowing the users to work much
faster. Siemens' Digital Enterprise segment helps to solve sustainability challenges by bringing the physical
and digital worlds together in a continuous data flow. The comprehensive digital twin is an important
aspect of that. It gathers information about products throughout their full lifecycle, from conception to
manufacturing and deployment. Siemens cutting-edge solutions enable the industry to better interpret this
data and make more efficient use of restricted resources.
Siemens operates in more than 200 countries. The company has a strong global presence, with R&D
centers in more than 39 countries that focus on creating innovative solutions. The company has offices in
the US, India, Germany, Singapore, China, Japan, South Korea, and Italy.

sections.heading: Business overview
content: Amazon divides its operations into three segments: Online Stores, Third-party Seller Services, Subscription
Services, Advertising Services, Physical Stores, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). Amazon Web Services Inc
(AWS) is a subsidiary of Amazon that provides cloud computing services. The company offers a
comprehensive range of cloud infrastructure services, including compute, storage, databases, analytics,
networking, mobile, developer tools, augmented reality and virtual reality, robotics, game tech, machine
learning, management tools, content delivery, media services, customer engagement, app streaming, and
security, identity, and compliance.
The company offers digital twin offerings through AWS. It has created a four-level digital twin index:
1−Descriptive, 2− Informative, 3−Predictive, and 4−Living Digital Twin.
L1−Descriptive concentrates on the physical system's engineering design and visual depiction (its
structure). A 2D engineering diagram (such as a process or piping and instrumentation diagram), a building
information model (BIM), or a complicated high-fidelity 3D/AR/VR model can be used for this purpose.
L2−Informative focuses on integrating IoT sensor and maintenance data from the physical system and
presenting it to the end user in a contextually appropriate manner, such as a 2D dashboard or a 3D
contextual visualization (e.g., its state). It allows the end user to comprehend the current state of the
physical system and includes rudimentary analytics that may be used to generate alarms.
L3−Predictive focuses on unmeasured quantity forecasts (e.g., virtual sensors, machine learning-based
anomaly detection), as well as employing predictive models to comprehend future states under ongoing
operations when future behavior is consistent with past behavior. These models can be scientific first
principles-based, data-driven (e.g., utilizing AI/ML), or a combination of the two.
L4−Living Digital Twin focuses on updatable models that can be aggregated to the fleet level if necessary.
According to AWS, the L4 level symbolizes the pinnacle of the digital twin journey. The ability for the model
to be updated depending on data from the physical entity and environment is the major difference
between L3 Predictive and L4 Living.
The company serves many industries, including automotive & transportation, infrastructure, healthcare, oil
& gas, energy & utilities, and retail. Amazon offers its digital twin services/solutions through AWS across all
the major regions, including Asia Pacific, the Americas, the Middle East, Africa, and Europe. The US, the
UK, Australia, China, France, Germany, India, Brazil, Canada, Ireland, Japan, Korea, and Singapore are
among a few major countries where AWS caters its services.

sections.heading: Business overview
content: ANSYS is a major player in engineering simulation software and services. The industry-leading portfolio of
engineering simulation software offered by ANSYS includes solutions for creating digital twins to analyze
real-time operational data to create awareness and facilitate faster decision-making while maximizing
machine efficiency in various industries. The company’s simulation tools create digital twins, which
optimize the operations of devices or systems. ANSYS’ Simplorer system-level modeling tool is used to
build digital twins that define the complex interaction between machine components, assemblies, and
subsystems accurately. ANSYS SCADE suite is a product line in the ANSYS embedded software family that
can be used to control a digital twin and develop a human–machine interface (HMI) using the same control
software. ANSYS 18 empowers users to create digital twins with the assistance of partner applications,
such as GE Predix and PTC ThingWorx.
Clients can use ANSYS Twin Builder to create comprehensive virtual prototypes of real-world systems.
These can be used to manage the whole product and asset lifecycle. This digital twin simulation paradigm
enables clients to boost savings exponentially over time by scheduling maintenance around predictive
approaches that improve with real-world testing and response. Engineers may use this data to extract more
value from existing assets, avoiding unplanned downtime and lowering operating costs while working at
peak efficiency, all while using agnostic Internet of Things (IoT) platforms.
ANSYS has more than 75 strategic sales locations worldwide, with a network of channel partners in more
than 40 countries. In addition, the company owns over 250 global partners that provide hardware,
connectivity, and software solutions that host or integrate with ANSYS software solutions. ANSYS also
collaborates with universities to help the academic institutes in utilizing ANSYS software in teaching and
research; ANSYS has over 3,300 university customers in 95 countries.

of business applications and analytics software in the digital commerce market. SAP Asset Intelligence
Network offered under the SAP Leonardo offering, which runs on the SAP Cloud Platform, creates digital
twins. SAP S/4HANA Cloud Platform, along with SAP IoT Application Enablement, offers microservices that
allow other systems to retrieve enhanced digital twin data, including business semantics, hierarchy data,
product master data, and customer contract documentation.
A digital twin can be established using a S/4HANA-enabled operational model to address the complete
breadth of finance and accounting, supply chain, procurement, master data for clients, and HR. The client's
cloud-based SAP S/4HANA operational environment model is enhanced with AI and integrated controls to
optimize the overall organization's efficiency and sustainability. Digital manufacturing requires the creation
and use of a digital twin based on Industrial IoT (IIoT). Companies that use SAP Intelligent Asset
Management can increase product quality, streamline manufacturing processes, and generate new
revenue streams. For firms that already use SAP solutions, using a digital twin via SAP IAM is even more
beneficial. This is because integration with existing SAP systems, such as enterprise resource planning
(ERP) or machine control in the form of manufacturing execution systems (MES), ensures that all necessary
processes, from purchasing to warehousing and actual production to after-sales services, mesh seamlessly
in the sense of networking from the top floor to shop floor.

sections.heading: Business overview
content: Robert Bosch is a global supplier of technology and services and is among the major players in the IoT
ecosystem. The company operates through four major business segments—Mobility Solutions, Industrial
Technology, Consumer Goods, and Energy and Building Technology. As a leading IoT provider, Bosch offers
solutions for smart homes, Industry 4.0, and connected mobility. Bosch offers smart home, Industry 4.0,
and linked mobility solutions. It leverages its expertise in sensor technology, software, services, and IoT
cloud to offers connected, cross-domain solutions from a single source.
The Bosch IoT cloud comprises three layers—SaaS, PaaS, and IaaS. According to Bosch, an IoT cloud
enables the creation of a digital twin of the physical asset based on readouts from machine components
as well as additional sensors. The digital twin in the Bosch IoT cloud is used to establish new application
areas, including automobile and industrial manufacturing. Bosch also offers digital buildings twin. In terms
of building management, the digital twin opens more options for the clients. A digital building twin will allow
for the creation of a virtual representation of a physical building, complete with all of the building's
systems, gadgets, sensors, and actuators. Bosch has the finest foundation for harnessing this potential
and establishing new services for its customers, owing to its many years of experience as a system
integrator and expertise in the field of IoT.
Robert Bosch and about 440 subsidiaries and regional firms are a part of the Bosch Group, which operates
in more than 60 countries. Bosch's global production, engineering, and sales network, which includes sales
and service partners, spans nearly every country worldwide. The company owns a network of more than 60
regional offices and 4,000 associates worldwide. The company offers products, solutions, and services in
major regions, including the Americas, Asia Pacific, and Europe. A few of the major regional offices of
Robert Bosch are located in the US, Germany, India, the Netherlands, Singapore, and Switzerland. Bosch
Rexroth (Germany), BSH Hausgeräte (Germany), Dremel (US), and ETAS (Germany) are few major
subsidiaries of the company.

content: Emerson operates through two core business platforms—Automation Solutions and
Commercial & Residential Solutions. The Automation Solutions segment of Emerson
offers digital twin solutions.
Emerson’s digital twin supports the needs of control system engineering, allowing
distributed teams access to system experts, regardless of location. It supports the
proven value of using dynamic simulation for designing, implementing, and testing
automation solutions. Emerson's digital twin solutions provide clairvoyance through
dynamic simulation software that simulates physical surroundings, allowing clients to
execute advanced testing and operator training without disrupting ongoing
operations. This reduces the expense and risk of enhancing operations for clients
while also increasing worker safety and upskilling. The Ovation digital twin
technology from Emerson ensures precise operator training, keeps up with process
changes, and validates control logic without disrupting plant operations. Ovation's
digital twin technology combines high-fidelity simulation with the control system,
allowing for real-time enhanced testing of innovative operational approaches in a
risk-free environment before they are implemented in the real plant. The virtual
platform-based digital twin simulator is an identical reproduction of the plant control
system. The difficulty and cost of maintaining separate modeling software are
eliminated with ovation-based models included in virtual controllers.

sections.heading: IOT SENSORS MARKET
content: Internet of things (IoT) sensors refer to sensors used in smart applications, which require uninterrupted
connectivity to carry out real-time data analytics. They require common connecting platforms for collecting
and analyzing data. IoT sensors are based on the computing concept that considers every physical object
to be connected to the Internet to communicate with each other. As IoT sensors are an integral component
of any digital twin solution, therefore IoT sensors are closely associated with digital twin.

sections.heading: INTRODUCTION
content: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a web of billions of machines that communicate with each other through
various long-range [for instance, cellular (LTE-A and LTE) and satellite] and short-range (for instance, RFID,
Wi-Fi, ZigBee, Bluetooth, Z-Wage, and Bluetooth Smart) communication technologies. The growth of IoT is
governed by its specialized applications in different markets such as healthcare, automotive, building
automation, and industrial. Each of these applications has varied bandwidth requirements, depending on
the coverage area, amount of data being transmitted, application, topology, power consumption, and data

sections.heading: load.
content: Connectivity technologies help IoT devices connect with each other as well as with the internet. The market
has seen an increase in the number of companies providing low-power wireless network connectivity
specifically designed for IoT applications. While introducing any new connectivity protocol and network
technology, it has to be mainly checked for short-range wireless communications, low power and energy
harvesting, real-time systems, radio-frequency identification, resource-constrained networks, and machine
type communication. The application developers and electronic engineers working on systems and
products for IoT have an extensive array of connectivity technologies available for their IoT devices. Thus, it
is important to understand the different technologies available to ensure the effective utilization of
technology for specific solutions or applications most efficiently and cost-effectively.

The growing demand for wireless data from mobile devices, connected cars, and smart grids, among
others, is creating the need for a more robust internet connection. Further, the proliferation of mobile
devices and the rapidly increasing adoption of the bring-your-own-device (BYOD) concept as well as IoT
within enterprises is expected to drive the growth of the market for wireless network technology. The
upcoming 5G mobile technology is expected to provide much faster internet connectivity and coverage,
which would also boost the market for wireless network technology.
Moreover, factors such as the growing adoption of cloud platforms and lower installation and maintenance
costs compared to wired devices are also likely to propel the adoption of wireless network technologies.
One of the major factors contributing to the growth of the market for wireless technology is the continuous
increase of internet users globally, which would strengthen the overall market for IoT. The use of cloud
computing is another factor fueling the growth of this market, which has advantages such as cost savings
in business operations. Organizations can save substantial capital costs required for in-house server
storage and other application requirements they maintain.
The huge adoption of Ethernet technology is a major contributor to the growth of the market for wired
technology. In 2021, Ethernet held the largest share of 49.7% of the wired technology market. The high
market share of this technology is attributed to its universal acceptance, growing use in industrial and
commercial buildings, and low cost. Moreover, it is cost-effective to produce controllers and I/O modules
that reside directly on Ethernet, providing the benefits of Ethernet connectivity without the need for
gateways, terminal servers, or other miscellaneous hardware.
